balance_notes: Finding 4 and 3, shipping_slice_reachable and launch_survives_itself: the flight block is rebuilt and the climb now completes. thrust_n 52000 over fuel_burn_kgs 18.6 is an exhaust velocity of 2795.7 m/s; wet mass 800 + 1600 = 2400 kg gives ideal dv = 2795.7 * ln(2400/800) = 3071 m/s at liftoff TWR 52000/(2400*9) = 2.41, inside the 1.4-2.6 band the audit read off its own reachable cluster. Flown, not argued: at the bottom sample both routes reach — orbit_reached true with 6.9% of tank left after circularising, arc_reached true with apex 73,749 m, a 125.9 s EVA window and 29.4% margin, against GDD 2.5's stated 29.5% and 97 s. The middle sample circularises at 2.9%; the top is arc-only (368 s window, 18.0% margin) and reports 'out of fuel before circularising', which is the progression beat GDD 2.5 asks for rather than a failure. The previous 105/70 vehicle died at 5,116 m because at 3.5 m2 of frontal area and 1.5 kg/m3 of sea-level density a 175 kg ship has no ballistic coefficient to spend; 2,400 kg wet does. climb_peak_heat is now a real measurement rather than a vacuous zero: 50.0 / 47.5 / 46.7 bar units on the three ascents, peaking at 19,459 m and 874 m/s — 47.5 at the middle sample reproduces GDD 2.2's stated ascent peak exactly — against heat_capacity 219, so the base ship survives its own launch with 77% of the bar unused and meets the mechanic somewhere it cannot kill it.

Finding 1, heavy_descent_requires_multi_pass, and the commit floor that makes it possible. reentry.commit_floor_m stays at GDD 2.2's stated 8,000 m: 35,000 m below atmosphere_top_m 43,000, so it genuinely constrains the entry, and 8 km above ground, so it is not the zero floor that turns the mechanic into a tax. Measured on committed_descents with the entry pinned there and the skim altitude scanned above it, all twelve rows: Armstrong's module plunges at 223.7 (bottom), 268.5 (middle), 335.5 (top) and comes home skimmed at 204.4 / 213.9 / 217.8, so its whole capacity window is (217.8, 223.7). The ladder is placed inside it — base heat_capacity 219, heat_shield tier 1 221, tier 2 223. Every tier is above 217.8, so a skimmed module survives at every shield the player can buy; every tier is below 223.7, so no purchase ever buys the plunge back. An empty ship plunges at 93.8 / 116.0 / 147.8 and a full hold at 104.3 / 128.6 / 163.4, both comfortably under 219 from anywhere in the band, so the inversion the last pass produced — ordinary cargo forced to aerobrake before the module — is gone: must_skim is false in all nine non-module rows and true in all three module rows. Two honest caveats. The window is 2.7% wide, not 32%: with the Researcher's drag_coefficient_shield 1.4 and this catalog it is the widest the physics offers, and I found it by scanning dry mass, which is the only parameter that moves it (at dry 900 the window is 0.8%, at 1,000 it is negative). And from the top of the band the module needs two skims, not one — at k=1 it peaks at 243.2, above every tier — so the finale is a three-cycle aerobraking descent. That is stricter than GDD 2.2's 'one skim, then commit' and the design should say so.

Finding 2, skim_multiplier_matches_flight: the flown array is adopted verbatim, and every number priced off it is recomputed. ablation.skim_heat_multiplier is [1.0, 0.405, 0.405, 0.405], which is skims.top.skim_heat_multiplier_measured for this vehicle entry for entry, delta 0.000 at all four indices. It is flat after index 1 because the flight is flat after index 1 — at these ballistic coefficients one skim at the scanned altitude drops apoapsis into the air and there is nothing left to shed — and 0.405 is well clear of the schema's 0.15 floor. The claimed [1, 0.71, 0.63, 0.60] of the last pass was pricing a benefit that was measured not to exist. The bottom and middle samples fly [1, 0.702, ...] and [1, 0.526, ...] and the schema has room for one array; I took the top's, because the top is where the binding case lives — the module hangs at 277,000 m and cannot plunge from anywhere. The cost is that the array overstates skimming at the bottom by about 1.7x, which is exactly why the bottom row's optimum is a near tie below.

GDD 2.2, the ablation model evaluated rather than asserted, so anyone can recompute cost_curve from the six constants. cost(sample,k) = SUM(i=0..k) 5.35 * 1.13^i + 7.0e-6 * (heat_index[sample] * skim_heat_multiplier[k])^3 + k * 7.0e-6 * 43.9^3. Per-cycle tolls are 5.350 / 6.046 / 6.831 / 7.719, cumulative 5.350 / 11.396 / 18.227 / 25.946. Each skim adds 7.0e-6 * 43.9^3 = 7.0e-6 * 84,605 = 0.592. Entry terms: bottom 7.000 at k=0 and 0.465 at k>=1 (40.50^3); middle 13.969 at k=0 (125.9^3 = 1,995,617) and 0.928 at k>=1 (50.99^3); top 29.706 at k=0 (161.9^3 = 4,243,660) and 1.973 at k>=1 (65.57^3). Summing gives bottom [12.35, 12.45, 19.88, 28.19], middle [19.32, 12.92, 20.34, 28.65], top [35.06, 13.96, 21.38, 29.70], so optimal_skims reads bottom 0, middle 1, top 1 — argmins of a curve, not targets. The bottom's 12.35 against 12.45 is a 0.8% tie, and it is a tie because the adopted top-sample multiplier flatters skimming down there; on the bottom's own flown 0.702 the k=1 cost would be 12.62 and the argmin would be 0 by a clearer margin. optimal_skims is a report either way and the design takes its multi-pass requirement from heat_capacity, not from this curve.

GDD 2.2, thermal fatigue as the whole brake, checked against the document's own 847% figure. cycle_toll_growth is 1.13, above 1 as the schema requires, with cycle_toll_base_pct 5.35. A 25-pass feathering descent is 24 skims plus one committed entry, so 25 heat cycles: SUM(i=0..24) 5.35 * 1.13^i = 5.35 * (1.13^25 - 1)/0.13 = 5.35 * 155.61 = 832.5% of plate, plus 24 skim terms at 0.592 = 14.2% and a 1.97% entry term, totalling 848.7% — GDD 2.2's '847% of plate, which is to say it is not available', reproduced to within 0.2% by two constants rather than quoted at. A flat toll would give 25 * 5.35 = 134% and would not stop anyone. A skim costs 0 m/s of dv and about six minutes, so this is the only thing bounding pass count, and it is priced as the whole brake.

GDD 2.3 and finding 5, the parachute: the GDD's stated canopy is restored and the speed is now a prediction the flight can contradict. parachute_area_m2 is back to the document's 630 at parachute_drag_coefficient 1.8 — the last pass shrank it 8.75x to 72 m2, which held 4.4 m/s fixed while the mass under it moved, and that is precisely the tautology the field was added to end. Against the Researcher's rho0 = 1.5 and g = 9.0, on the full-hold mass the sweep computes (dry 800 + 6 slots at 30.43 kg = 182.6, so 982.6 kg): v = sqrt(2 * 982.6 * 9.0 / (1.5 * 1.8 * 630)) = sqrt(17,686.8 / 1,701) = sqrt(10.398) = 3.23 m/s. Flown, the integrator lands the full hold at 3.22 m/s at all three sample altitudes — delta 0.01 m/s, 0.3% of the claim, with independent true. It is under the 5.0 soft line but also under the ~3.5 the audit wants for headroom, by 0.28 m/s, and that is a catalog consequence rather than a choice: see catalog_concerns. Armstrong's module lands at 6.83 m/s on the base canopy, hard enough to degrade it one state, so the Parachute track is what buys the win condition rather than what buys ordinary landings — tier 1 (900 m2) gives 5.71 m/s, still hard; tier 2 (1,250 m2) gives 4.84 m/s, soft, and a pristine delivery. That is GDD 2.6's 'landable only near full upgrades' expressed as a canopy.

Finding 5, no_target_moved_to_pass, and the one quantity I could not satisfy without moving something that is not mine. Three GDD-stated numbers are restored or held: parachute_area_m2 630 and parachute_drag_coefficient 1.8 (GDD 2.3), cargo.base_slots 6 and eva.base_tether_slots 2 (GDD 2.4, 2.5), reentry.commit_floor_m 8,000 (GDD 2.2). dry_mass_kg is set at 800 by the two constraints the audit named — staged ballistic coefficient 800 / (1.4 * 3.5) = 163.3 kg/m2, above the Researcher's floor of 100 and far above the ~50 cliff where first contact erases the orbit rather than trimming it, and the capacity window above, which closes entirely at dry mass 950 and beyond. It is NOT set to make GDD 2.5's full-hold doubling read 2.00x; that rule now reads 982.6 / 800 = 1.23x and is reported as broken rather than satisfied from dry mass, which is what the audit asked for. Making it true would require dry_mass_kg 183, which gives a staged ballistic coefficient of 37 — below the aerobraking cliff, so the skim mechanic and the ascent both disappear, which is exactly the failure the last pass shipped. Two GDD quantities cannot both be true of this vehicle; the resolution here is to keep the flyable one and name the other.

GDD 2.5, a lazy run breaks even, computed from the catalog rather than asserted. A piece's multiplier is 1.0 + 4.5 * (altitude_m - 50,000) / 230,000. The three cheapest hand-tetherable pieces off the floor are crumpled_panel_stack (56,000 m, small, x1.117) at 44.70, spent_kick_motor_casing (73,500 m, x1.460) at 58.39 and seized_reaction_wheel_housing (106,000 m, x2.096) at 83.83 — two of them are 103.1 and three are 186.9, and launch_cost 110 sits between, which is GDD 2.5's 'the value of two to three cheap pieces' read straight off this catalog. A lazy six-slot run of panel stacks grosses 268.2 against 110 for the stage and 12.35% of plate at replate_cost_per_pct 2 = 24.7, netting 133.5; swap one panel for a bent_truss_section (119.93, two slots) and it nets 164. Even at the tow fee's 50% clamp the run lands at break-even rather than negative, which is what the clamp is for, and the mercy floor covers the rest. One intact cracked_solar_array (61,500 m, medium, fragile) is 90 * 1.225 * 3.0 = 330.8 on its own — more than the entire six-panel haul — so fragile_value_premium 3.0 reshapes a run's payout exactly as the charter asks.

GDD 2.4, no shear under steady tow, proved as a bound rather than case by case. Steady cable tension is m_piece * a with a = jetpack_thrust_n / (suit_mass_kg + total towed), so tension = 520 * m / (110 + M), which is strictly below jetpack_thrust_n = 520 N at every load and every tether count — towed mass suppresses acceleration faster than it loads the cable, so the bound holds for any catalog whatever. magnet_hold_force_n is 900 N, a 1.73x margin everywhere, so shear can only fire on latch jerk and swing jerk, which is what GDD 2.4 says it is for. Worst real cases: the two heaviest shipping-slice pieces (dead_thruster_quad 70 kg plus shattered_star_tracker 72 kg) put 148.6 N on the cable at 2.06 m/s2; Armstrong's 3,600 kg module puts 388.2 N at 0.140 m/s2, still 2.3x under the hold force, and at 0.35 kg/s a 24 kg jetpack tank buys 68.6 s of continuous thrust for that haul. A bare suit accelerates at 4.73 m/s2 and a two-piece mid-band tow at 2.06 — a 2.3x penalty, heavy enough to be a decision and light enough to fly. The hand_magnet tiers buy magnet_range_screens (0.125 to 0.1875 to 0.25) rather than hold force, per GDD 2.4's mass-neutral promise.

GDD 2.2, why heat_index and the capacity ladder are different numbers on the same bar, because reading one as the other is how the last audit's evidence and mine can look contradictory. heat_index is the peak of a DIRECT entry at periapsis 0 with an empty hold, normalised so the bottom sample reads 100 — bottom 100.0, middle 125.9, top 161.9 — because that periapsis-0 basis is the one the skim study shares, and the product heat_index * skim_heat_multiplier only means anything if both come off the same basis. skim_peak 43.9 is measured on the same basis: the peak of the skim pass itself, empty ship, top of the band. The capacity ladder is measured somewhere else — at commit_floor_m 8,000 m, the shallowest entry a player may legally fly, where the top's empty-ship entry reads 147.8 against 161.9 at depth 0. Neither is wrong. A periapsis-0 entry is not a legal descent, so it prices the skim model and does not set the capacity.

GDD 2.5, the shop, priced against runs rather than listed. The twelve purchases total 10,150. Net profit per run at the tier that buys them: a floor run nets 133-165, a mid-band run of three torn_solar_wing_spars (131,000 m, x2.585, 232.7 each) nets 562 after launch and replating, and a maxed ten-slot top-band run of scorched_fuel_cell_stacks (242,500 m, x4.766, 429 each) nets about 2,000 — so 12-15 runs clear the shop with three to five budgeted failures still funded, which is GDD 2.5's pacing target. The tank and thruster tiers are sized as a pair because apex is thrust-limited: base 52,000 N on 2,400 kg is TWR 2.41, tank tier 1 (2,400 kg) with thruster tier 1 (64,000 N) on 3,200 kg is 2.22, tank tier 2 (3,000 kg) with thruster tier 2 (75,000 N) on 3,800 kg is 2.19. Flown, tank tier 1 turns the top of the band from arc-only into a real orbit — circularising at 215,000 m with about 12% of tank left where the base ship cannot circularise there at all — which is GDD 2.5's 'the buy that turns a hop into a stay', one band higher than the document places it.

Two things I could not fix from here, stated rather than tuned around. (1) GDD 2.5 makes the heat shield the only mass-reducing purchase — the systemic counterweight to storage-driven landing difficulty — but the upgrades schema carries one effect per entry and the charter requires heat_shield to buy heat_capacity, so dry_mass_kg stays 800 at every tier and the counterweight in this value set is Parachute. (2) GDD 2.6 says value scales with mass on top of the altitude gradient; economy has only size_class_base_value and the gradient, no mass term, so a 112 kg cracked_command_module_hatch (small, 268,000 m) prices at 190.6 while a 78 kg cracked_deep_space_dish (medium, fragile, 217,500 m) prices at 986.7. The catalog's masses do rise with altitude so the gradient carries the intent approximately, but the coupling the GDD claims is not in these numbers.
catalog_concerns: The shipping slice's mass per slot, against GDD 2.5's full-hold doubling and GDD 2.3's parachute margin at the same time. Spawn-weighted over the bottom two thirds, hand-tetherable only, at compactor_tier 1, the catalog prices out at 30.43 kg per slot, so six base slots is a 182.6 kg hold. For GDD 2.5's 'a full hold roughly doubles the rocket's mass' to be true, dry_mass_kg would have to be 183 — a staged ballistic coefficient of 37, below the ~50 cliff where the atmosphere stops the ship instead of braking it, which deletes the skim mechanic and crashes the ascent. I balanced against the catalog as it stands and left the rule broken at 1.23x rather than satisfy it from dry mass. The same shortfall costs the parachute its headroom: at 630 m2 and Cd 1.8 the full hold lands at 3.23 m/s, 0.28 m/s under the ~3.5 the audit wants, because there is not enough cargo mass to load the canopy. Both close at once if the slice averages about 133 kg per slot — a full hold would then be 800 kg on an 800 kg ship, exactly 2.00x, and land at 4.11 m/s, in the middle of the soft band. That is a 4.4x raise on the pieces below 203,333 m and it is a much bigger ask than the 2.2x of the last revision; the honest alternative, if the floor cannot carry that, is for the GDD to withdraw the doubling sentence, because no dry mass satisfies it and the flight at once.

Storage tier 2 has no effect on landing difficulty, which is the pair GDD 2.5 designs around. At 30.43 kg per slot, going from 6 slots to 10 adds 121.7 kg to a 800 kg ship and moves the full-hold touchdown from 3.23 to 3.42 m/s — both soft, on the base canopy, with no purchase required. GDD 2.5's 'storage raises the profit ceiling and the difficulty of the flight home' is currently only the first half: the profit ceiling rises 67%, the difficulty does not move. This is the same per-slot mass finding as above seen from the shop's side, and it is why Armstrong's module rather than a maxed hold is doing all of the Parachute track's work.

armstrongs_module at 3,600 kg against the heaviest ordinary piece, recorded as a property to protect rather than a defect. severed_boom_mast at 165 kg is 21.8x lighter and impact_pitted_engine_bell at 122 kg is the heaviest the magnet can legally take, so the module is 4.5x a maxed ten-slot hold on its own. That ratio is what keeps every ordinary haul under 164 on the bar while the module plunges at 223.7-335.5, and it is the only reason a capacity window exists at all — at drag_coefficient_shield 1.4 that window is (217.8, 223.7), 2.7% wide, and it closes from below the moment the top of the catalog drifts toward a full hold's mass. If a future pass rescales masses, the quantity to hold is module_mass / (base_slots * shipping_slice_mean), currently 19.7.
